statement: The system shall provide better visibility so managers and staff can make faster, more informed decisions about collections, staffing, space, patron needs, and financial activity.

The system shall provide the consortium level with a clearer picture of how libraries are performing together so it can spot trends, compare branches fairly, and support planning without interrupting day-to-day service.
Success shall be measured by whether people actually use the reports to make decisions, obtain needed information without a lot of manual work, and trust the data enough to guide action.
Consortium oversight shall include more consistent reporting across libraries and a better ability to identify issues or opportunities early.
Local branch staff shall be able to view and generate the reports they need for day-to-day work.
Local branch staff shall not be able to access broader system-wide or sensitive financial views unless specifically authorized.
Managers and directors shall have wider access for their own branches or systems.
Managers and directors shall have access to more detailed operational and performance reports.
Directors shall be able to access comparative views across branches they oversee.
Consortium administrators shall have the broadest access for system-wide oversight.
Consortium administrators shall have access to cross-branch reporting and higher-level financial or usage summaries.
Permissions shall be role-based and may be scoped by branch or region.
Access shall be restricted for patron-level data and financial details so users only see what they need for their job.
Most reports shall be available on demand.
Standard operational and consortium reports shall refresh on a schedule.
Users shall be able to access reports through a dashboard for quick viewing.
Users shall be able to download reports for sharing or further analysis.
Email delivery shall be available for scheduled summaries or alerts.

The default report grouping shall match how each role works.
Different report types should have different retention periods.
Operational reports should generally be retained for a shorter, recent period because they are mainly used for recent decision-making.
Collection data should be retained over a longer window than operational and staffing reports.
Financial reports should be retained for the longest period because of audit and planning needs.
Collection and trend data should be retained after financial records and before routine operational snapshots are discarded.
Routine operational snapshots may be rolled off sooner than other retained data.
The chosen retention policy should support year-over-year comparison.
The chosen retention policy should support required audit needs.
The chosen retention policy should support required public records needs.
